assertions.name: the_lattice_window_is_converged
assertions.source: widening the lattice window from 3 to 5 moves the energy by 0.0 relative -- the nearest-translate minimisation is saturated, so the reported energies are not window artifacts

assertions.name: the_integrand_is_IDENTICALLY_zero_near_the_diagonal
assertions.source: worst residual 0.0 over four decades approaching the diagonal. On a flat torus the nearest lattice translate of a short geodesic arc is 0, so d_ambient = |u| = d_arc EXACTLY and O'Hara's regularisation cancels on the nose. That is what makes this computable without a principal value

assertions.name: the_energy_is_scale_and_therefore_q0_independent
assertions.source: three scales spanning 1e-1 to 1e3 agree to 2.216e-41 relative. Moebius energy is scale-invariant, so the ln q0 prefactor of the log-holonomy DROPS OUT. Consequence: this energy cannot be the 'evaluated at q_0' quantity the 2026-08-01 method redirect asked for -- it does not see q0 at all

assertions.name: every_energy_is_non_negative
assertions.source: min over candidates = 22.4666084053. O'Hara energy is an integral of `1/d_ambient^2 - 1/d_arc^2` with `d_ambient <= d_arc` pointwise, so it cannot be negative. The first build of this probe returned ~-4e44 here -- catastrophic cancellation at the endpoints, where the integrand is analytically zero and was being evaluated as 1e80 - 1e80. This assertion and [C3] are what caught it

assertions.name: the_cusp_torus_class_is_writhe_and_strands_only
assertions.source: all 4 two-crossing dressings map to the single class (2, 3). m is the exponent sum (a sum over letters) and l is the strand count (independent of the word), so the class is a letter-sum-type invariant by construction

assertions.name: the_bridge_TIES_the_candidates_it_was_built_to_separate
assertions.source: one distinct O'Hara energy over 4 candidates. The same tie crossing count and crossing energy already failed on, reached by a third and independent route. The O'Hara functional is innocent: the CUSP-TORUS EMBEDDING is the lossy step, and it provably forgets the knot

assertions.name: this_does_NOT_retract_the_green_light
assertions.source: qbeta_embedding_energy_can_discriminate (5/5) showed the four candidates are DISTINCT LINKS, so an isotopy-class functional is not barred from separating them. That stands. This probe shows only that the cusp-torus winding class is too coarse an embedding to realise it -- a statement about the embedding, not about the energy

description: Builds the Bring->O'Hara bridge and reports what it gives. CORRECTS my own claim (bean qou-pzsi, PR #7370) that the corpus has no braid-word to curve map: qbeta_cusp_lattice_geodesic_probe carries it, filed under GEODESIC, on the author's steering of 2026-07-27. What was genuinely missing is the geodesic -> O'Hara energy step, implemented here: on a flat torus a geodesic is straight in the universal cover, so the ambient and arc distances are both closed-form and the O'Hara subtraction cancels EXACTLY (the integrand is identically zero near the diagonal, not merely integrable). Half A is derived: m = exponent sum from the proved meridian-holonomy boost, l = strand count from the closure. RESULT, a negative: (m, l) = (writhe, strands) are both letter-sum-type, so all four two-crossing gluon dressings share one class, one geodesic and one energy -- the same tie, by a third route. The O'Hara energy is innocent; the cusp-torus embedding is the lossy step, and it provably forgets the knot. Also measured: the energy is scale- hence q0-INDEPENDENT, so it cannot be the 'evaluated at q_0' quantity the 2026-08-01 redirect asked for.

bridge.half_A_word_to_class: m = exponent sum (meridian-holonomy-boost.md: one meridian turn is a boost of rapidity ln q0, and a positive crossing carries the Hecke eigenvalue q); l = strand count (the closure wraps the axis once per strand). Both forced.
bridge.half_B_class_to_geodesic: u_{m,l} = ln q0 * (m + l*omega) on the flat cusp torus C/Lambda, Lambda = Z<1, omega>, omega = e^{i pi/3} -- the corpus's own map (qbeta_cusp_lattice_geodesic_probe)
bridge.half_C_geodesic_to_energy: E = L * int_0^L [1/d_ambient(u)^2 - 1/d_arc(u)^2] du, with d_ambient the flat-torus distance (min over lattice translates) and d_arc = min(u, L-u). NEW.

verdict.reading: the cusp-torus winding class is (writhe, strands), both letter-sum-type, so this bridge inherits the blindness that defeated crossing count and crossing energy
verdict.what_survives: the green light -- the candidates ARE distinct links, so a FINER embedding is not excluded. The genus-4 Bring curve itself is not used here; only the genus-1 cusp torus the corpus's braid map lands in
verdict.separate_finding: the energy is scale- hence q0-independent, so it cannot be the 'evaluated at q_0' quantity the 2026-08-01 method redirect asked for

corrects.qou-pzsi / PR #7370: 'no map from a braid word to a curve in or on the Bring surface' is WRONG -- qbeta_cusp_lattice_geodesic_probe carries it, filed under GEODESIC. My searches keyed on embed/curve/parametrise near 'bring' and on consumers of the Moebius integrators, and the map was one word away from every one of them

that no finer Bring embedding exists -- the genus-4 curve is unused here
that any candidate should be adopted
